expert_proposals.title: Reverse cost-model direction: raise random_page_cost 1.5->3.0, seq_page_cost 0.8->1.0
expert_proposals.configuration_cause: GetUserTweets consumes 87.6% of terminal capacity at p50 138us; the incumbent's cache-optimistic cost model (random_page_cost 1.5, seq_page_cost 0.8) was set by the refuted r007 direction, and the r008 upward reversal was never executed. Cost-model calibration is the only in-scope lever that can change the GetUserTweets access path without touching WAL or predicate locks.
expert_proposals.mechanism: GetUserTweets dominates terminal time (87.6% capacity, p50 138us, p95 200us). The incumbent cost model is cache-optimistic (random_page_cost 1.5, seq_page_cost 0.8), a direction already refuted at r007. Raising random_page_cost to 3.0 and seq_page_cost to 1.0 (PostgreSQL defaults) re-prices random index probes relative to sequential scans, so the planner may pick a cheaper path for the skewed user_id lookup and shrink pages touched per call. This is a bounded reversal of a falsified direction, not a replay of the WAL bundle.
expert_proposals.query_effect: GetUserTweets is a single-table lookup by user_id; raising random_page_cost makes the planner prefer a sequential or bitmap path when the index probe is estimated expensive, potentially reducing per-call page touches for skewed users.
expert_proposals.expected_tps_effect: Small increase (>=0.3%) if the access path improves; unchanged if the plan is already optimal.
expert_proposals.expected_latency_effect: GetUserTweets p50/p95 decrease by >=1% if the path changes; unchanged otherwise.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Raise from incumbent 1.5 toward PostgreSQL default 4.0; 3.0 is within safe [1.0,6.0] and is a larger amplitude than the untested r008 value 2.5, reversing the refuted r007 direction (1.5->1.1).
knob_changes.mechanism_role: planner cost of random/cached reads; raising it discourages random index probes

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Raise from 0.8 to PostgreSQL default 1.0, within safe [0.5,2.0]; paired with random_page_cost to keep the random/seq ratio at 3.0.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: I/O cost scale paired with random_page_cost; raising it rebalances toward sequential paths

predictions.rationale: Re-priced random reads may select a cheaper path for the dominant lookup.
Tail follows the same path change; p95 200us has headroom.
Freed terminal capacity from the 87.6% dominant transaction raises completed TPS.

alternatives.statement: If the planner already uses the optimal Index Scan for GetUserTweets, the cost-model change leaves the plan and latency unchanged, and TPS stays flat.
If WAL sync (0.11ms average) rather than query path limits throughput, GetUserTweets latency is unchanged and only WAL knobs would move TPS.

expert_proposals.why_exceeds_incumbent: The incumbent's cost model is cache-optimistic from a refuted direction; restoring PostgreSQL-default costs is a bounded, untested reversal that can only help if the GetUserTweets plan is suboptimal, and is neutral otherwise.

nodes.label: Re-priced random vs sequential reads may select cheaper GetUserTweets path

expert_proposals.title: Reverse group-commit window: commit_delay 100->0, commit_siblings 2->8, wal_writer_flush_after 0->128
expert_proposals.configuration_cause: Incumbent carries commit_delay=100us with commit_siblings=2 and wal_writer_flush_after=0. The r010 test (commit_delay 500, siblings 3, flush_after 256) was inconclusive on sync latency and refuted on TPS: the wider window added fixed per-commit stall without coalescing fsyncs (sync_average_ms stayed ~0.10-0.11ms, wal_waiting_backends.max still 1-3). The fixed sleep is pure added latency at 5 terminals; the writer-side flush batching was never actually engaged because flush_after=0 disables it.
expert_proposals.mechanism: At 5 terminals the group-commit window cannot collect enough siblings to amortize its fixed sleep, so commit_delay is a pure per-commit tax. Reversing to commit_delay=0 removes the stall; raising commit_siblings to 8 keeps the (now zero) window inactive so no accidental sleep returns. Setting wal_writer_flush_after=128 (1MB) engages background writer flush batching so WAL writes are coalesced on the writer side rather than per-write, reducing wal_waiting_backends queueing without gating foreground commits. This is the opposite direction of the refuted r010 amplitude and targets the writer path, not the commit sleep.
expert_proposals.query_effect: InsertTweet commit path loses the fixed 100us sleep; GetUserTweets read path unaffected.
expert_proposals.expected_tps_effect: Small increase (0.3-1%) if the commit sleep was a real tax; neutral if WAL sync is already fully amortized.
expert_proposals.expected_latency_effect: InsertTweet p95 should drop by the removed sleep; overall p95 roughly unchanged.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Safe low bound 0; r010 showed 500us window refuted sync reduction and inconsistent TPS, so reverse to 0 to eliminate the fixed per-commit stall.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: group-commit collection window; 0 disables the fixed sleep

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Raise from 2 to 8 within safe [0,20]; with 5 terminals, 8 siblings means the (zero) window never activates, preventing accidental stall.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: group-commit activation threshold; high value keeps window inactive

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Set from 0 to 128 (8kB units = 1MB) within safe [0,1024]; engages writer-side flush batching so background writer coalesces WAL writes without gating foreground commits.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: writer flush batch size; batches background WAL writes

predictions.rationale: Removing the 100us fixed commit_delay sleep should lower InsertTweet p95.
Writer-side flush batching at 128 (1MB) should reduce WAL wait queueing versus per-write flushing.
Removing the commit sleep frees terminal capacity for completed transactions.

alternatives.statement: If WAL sync is already fully amortized, removing commit_delay yields no measurable TPS change and the writer flush batching is the only lever.
If the fixed sleep was masking a real fsync bottleneck, removing it raises wal_waiting_backends and sync_average_ms.

expert_proposals.why_exceeds_incumbent: Incumbent pays a fixed 100us commit sleep that r010 showed cannot be amortized at 5 terminals, and disables writer flush batching (flush_after=0). Reversing to commit_delay=0 with commit_siblings=8 removes the tax and engages writer-side batching, a direction not yet tested.

nodes.label: Remove fixed commit sleep; engage writer-side flush batching

expert_proposals.title: Restore page/relation predicate-lock caps to defaults to cut SIRead promotion churn
expert_proposals.configuration_cause: Incumbent sets max_pred_locks_per_page=0 and max_pred_locks_per_relation=0, forcing immediate promotion of every page/relation SIRead lock to coarser granularity; this maximizes promotion churn and lock bookkeeping per GetUserTweets transaction (87.6% of terminal capacity).
expert_proposals.mechanism: With max_pred_locks_per_page=0 and max_pred_locks_per_relation=0, PostgreSQL promotes SIRead locks to the coarsest granularity immediately, generating extra lock-manager work and lock-table churn on every GetUserTweets scan. Restoring the PostgreSQL defaults (page=2, relation=-2) keeps fine-grained SIRead locks longer, reducing promotion events and lock bookkeeping per transaction. Because GetUserTweets consumes 87.6% of finite terminal time, any per-transaction lock overhead reduction directly frees terminal capacity for more successful transactions. This is a distinct direction from the previously refuted 2->8/2->32 raises and the untested 0 extreme; it tests the default midpoint of the granularity axis.
expert_proposals.query_effect: GetUserTweets index scans retain fine-grained SIRead locks instead of immediate promotion, reducing lock-manager work per call.
expert_proposals.expected_tps_effect: Small increase (>=0.3%) if promotion churn is a real per-transaction cost; unchanged if lock bookkeeping is not on the critical path.
expert_proposals.expected_latency_effect: GetUserTweets p99 should decrease slightly; p50 unchanged.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: PostgreSQL default 2, within safe [0,256]; reverses incumbent 0 extreme toward default midpoint.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: page-level predicate-lock granularity cap; higher value delays promotion to coarser granularity

knob_changes.numerical_basis: PostgreSQL default -2, within safe [-2,4096]; reverses incumbent 0 extreme toward default.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: relation-level predicate-lock granularity cap; -2 uses default fraction of per-txn budget

predictions.rationale: Restoring default caps keeps fine-grained SIRead locks longer, reducing promotion events and total lock count.
Less lock-manager work per GetUserTweets call lowers tail latency.
Freed terminal capacity from reduced per-transaction lock overhead raises successful TPS.

alternatives.statement: If lock bookkeeping is not on the critical path, locks_total.p95 may not decrease and TPS stays flat; the mechanism is then refuted and the granularity axis is exhausted.
If WAL sync latency dominates, restoring predicate-lock defaults will not move TPS; wal_timing.sync_average_ms would remain the binding constraint.

unverified interaction note (demoted to pending constraint): wal_writer_flush_after
expert_proposals.why_exceeds_incumbent: Incumbent sits at the coarsest SIRead extreme (0/0), which maximizes promotion churn. Restoring defaults tests the opposite direction on the same axis with a bounded, low-risk amplitude, and directly targets the 87.6% terminal-capacity transaction.

nodes.label: Default SIRead granularity reduces promotion churn and lock bookkeeping per GetUserTweets
